section_summary: This section comprises correspondence and memoranda from June 1940 to February 1941 concerning Japanese government officials, military officers, railway personnel, and academic researchers stationed in or departing from the United States. The records primarily consist of diplomatic notes from the Japanese Embassy and Japanese Chargé d'Affaires requesting Federal income tax exemptions and sailing permits under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for naval inspectors, language officers, railway officials, and scholars. They also contain formal State Department certifications of reciprocity directed to the Secretary of the Treasury, Treasury responses confirming tax-exempt treatment, and an Office of Naval Intelligence report concerning Japanese naval fuel inspection operations.

subfiles.about: Transmits an ONI report regarding the closure of the Japanese Naval Fuel Inspection Office in Los Angeles and the reported establishment of an oil inspection office in Mexico.
subfiles.from: E. B. Nixon, Captain, U.S. Navy, Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.summary: Captain E. B. Nixon of the Office of Naval Intelligence forwards a report from the Eleventh Naval District to Fletcher Warren of the State Department. The report notes that following the Japanese Ambassador's notification of the closure of the Japanese Naval Fuel Inspection Office in Los Angeles, an unidentified Japanese individual arrived from San Francisco and met with office personnel. The individual stated he was on a three-year assignment, was departing for Mexico on May 4, 1940, and reported that an oil inspection office would be established in Mexico.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Japanese Naval Fuel Inspection Office in Los Angeles

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure of Tamon Maeda, a technical expert of the Japanese Foreign Office assigned to The Japan Institute in New York, and requests tax exemption notifications.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State that Mr. Tamon Maeda, a technical expert of the Foreign Office assigned to The Japan Institute in New York City, will depart the United States. Maeda, who arrived in Seattle on October 19, 1938 on the Heian Maru, is scheduled to sail from San Francisco on June 24, 1940 aboard the Asama Maru. The Ambassador requests that Maeda's departure and tax-exempt status be communicated to the appropriate United States authorities.
subfiles.title: Note No. 137 from the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Departure of Tamon Maeda

subfiles.about: Certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Tamon Maeda is entitled to Federal income tax exemption on his official compensation.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull writes to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. regarding the desired Federal income tax exemption for Tamon Maeda, a technical expert of the Japanese Foreign Office. Hull confirms a telephone message sent to the Bureau of Internal Revenue on June 12, 1940, noting that Maeda plans to leave New York on June 15 and sail from San Francisco on June 24 on the Asama Maru. In accordance with Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Hull certifies that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. government employees performing similar services in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Tamon Maeda
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 137 and informs the Japanese Ambassador that steps have been taken to issue a sailing permit and grant income tax exemption to Tamon Maeda.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 137 of June 8, 1940 regarding Tamon Maeda's income tax exemption. The note confirms that, following a telephone request from the Embassy on June 12, the matter of issuing a sailing permit prior to Maeda's departure from New York on June 15 was referred to the competent U.S. authorities. The Department states that appropriate action would be taken promptly to issue the sailing permit and exempt Maeda from Federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Ambassador Concerning Sailing Permit and Tax Exemption for Tamon Maeda

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure from the United States of Assistant Engineer Toshiyuki Mori of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State of the upcoming departure of Mr. Toshiyuki Mori, an Assistant Engineer and Assistant Inspector of the Naval Technical Department stationed at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. Mori, whose income is derived solely from the Japanese Government, is scheduled to leave Seattle on July 22, 1940 aboard the steamship Heian Maru. The Ambassador requests that Mori's departure and tax-exempt status be brought to the attention of appropriate United States authorities. (Includes duplicate copy on page 88).
subfiles.title: Note No. 141 from the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Departure of Toshiyuki Mori

subfiles.about: File copy of the certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code regarding Federal income tax exemption for Tamon Maeda.
subfiles.summary: This document is a file carbon copy of the Secretary of State's letter to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., confirming the June 12 telephone message to the Bureau of Internal Revenue regarding Tamon Maeda. It provides formal certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that the Japanese Government grants reciprocal income tax exemptions to U.S. government employees in Japan. Maeda was scheduled to leave New York on June 15 and sail from San Francisco on June 24 on the Asama Maru.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Tamon Maeda (Copy)
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: File copy of the State Department's note acknowledging Note No. 137 regarding Tamon Maeda's sailing permit and tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: This document is a file copy of the Department of State's note to the Japanese Ambassador acknowledging note no. 137 of June 8, 1940 regarding Mr. Tamon Maeda. It states that the Embassy's telephone request of June 12 for an expedited sailing permit before Maeda's departure from New York on June 15 was brought to the attention of competent authorities. The note confirms that prompt action was arranged to issue the permit and ensure exemption from Federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Ambassador Concerning Sailing Permit and Tax Exemption for Tamon Maeda (Copy)

subfiles.about: Encloses Japanese Embassy Note No. 141 and certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Toshiyuki Mori.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Note No. 141 from the Japanese Ambassador concerning the tax exemption of Mr. Toshiyuki Mori. Mori served as Assistant Engineer and Assistant Inspector of the Naval Technical Department at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City and planned to depart Seattle on July 22 aboard the Heian Maru. Hull certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent tax exemptions to American officials performing similar duties in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Toshiyuki Mori
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 141 and confirms transmittal of Toshiyuki Mori's tax exemption request to U.S. tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 141 of June 13, 1940 regarding Mr. Toshiyuki Mori of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York. The note informs the Ambassador that a copy of his communication has been forwarded to the competent U.S. authorities. This action was taken to facilitate Mori's exemption from Federal income tax prior to his departure from Seattle on July 22 aboard the SS Heian Maru.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Ambassador Concerning Tax Exemption for Toshiyuki Mori

subfiles.about: Confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials granting income tax exemption to Tamon Maeda.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury replies to the Secretary of State's letter of June 18, 1940 certifying the tax-exempt status of Tamon Maeda under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. The letter notes Maeda's role as a technical expert of the Japanese Foreign Office and his planned departure from San Francisco on June 24 after leaving New York on June 15. The Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to the Internal Revenue officials concerned to grant the requested tax exemption and facilitate his sailing permit.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Tamon Maeda

subfiles.about: Acknowledges certification under Section 116(h) and confirms instructions to Internal Revenue officials regarding Toshiyuki Mori.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of June 21, 1940 regarding Mr. Toshiyuki Mori of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. The letter confirms receipt of the State Department's reciprocity certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. Treasury informs the Department of State that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials regarding Mori's tax exemption in connection with his departure from Seattle on July 22.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Toshiyuki Mori

subfiles.about: Transmits the biographical records of Lieutenant Colonel Takekatu Endo and Major Takeo Kato, newly arrived language officers of the Imperial Japanese Army.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents his compliments to the Secretary of State and encloses the biographical records of Lieutenant Colonel Takekatu Endo and Major Takeo Kato. Both officers are newly arrived language officers of the Imperial Japanese Army assigned to duty in the United States. The attached records were subsequently detached for administrative filing within the State Department.
subfiles.title: Note No. 162 from the Japanese Ambassador Transmitting Biographical Records of Takekatu Endo and Takeo Kato

subfiles.about: Requests Federal income tax exemption for four Japanese naval language officers attached to the Naval Attaché's Office in Washington, D.C.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that four Japanese naval officers attached to the Japanese Naval Attaché's Office at 3700 Massachusetts Avenue in Washington, D.C. be granted exemption from income taxes. The accompanying schedule lists Engineer Lieutenant Commander Kazuo Imai, Lieutenant Commander Yuzuru Sanematsu, Engineer Lieutenant Magoto Takita, and Lieutenant Commander Sadatomo Okada. The Ambassador requests that their names be forwarded to the appropriate United States tax authorities. (Includes duplicate copy on page 101).
subfiles.title: Note No. 171 from the Japanese Ambassador Requesting Tax Exemption for Naval Language Officers

subfiles.about: Encloses Japanese Embassy Note No. 171 and certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for four naval language officers.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of State transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Note No. 171 from the Japanese Embassy with its attached list of language officers. The officers, attached to the Japanese Naval Attaché's Office in Washington, D.C., include Kazuo Imai, Yuzuru Sanematsu, Magoto Takita, and Sadatomo Okada. The State Department certifies under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that reciprocal tax exemption privileges are extended to American government employees in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Four Japanese Naval Language Officers
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 171 and confirms transmittal of the tax exemption request for four naval language officers to U.S. authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Department of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 171 of July 29, 1940 concerning income tax exemption for four language officers attached to the Japanese Naval Attaché's Office. The note informs the Ambassador that a copy of the request has been transmitted to competent U.S. government authorities to secure the desired exemptions. The officers covered by this action are Kazuo Imai, Yuzuru Sanematsu, Magoto Takita, and Sadatomo Okada.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Ambassador Concerning Tax Exemption for Four Naval Language Officers

subfiles.about: Duplicate file copy of Note No. 162 transmitting biographical records of Lieutenant Colonel Takekatu Endo and Major Takeo Kato.
subfiles.summary: This page is an identical duplicate copy of Note No. 162 from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State dated July 16, 1940. It transmits the biographical records of Lieutenant Colonel Takekatu Endo and Major Takeo Kato, newly arrived language officers of the Imperial Japanese Army. Notations show receipt by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs and subsequent filing.
subfiles.title: Note No. 162 from the Japanese Ambassador Transmitting Biographical Records of Takekatu Endo and Takeo Kato (Duplicate)

subfiles.about: Encloses Japanese Embassy Note No. 180 and certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Sigeyoshi Sakabe and Isao Ashida of The Japan Institute.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull writes to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., enclosing a copy of Note No. 180 of August 6, 1940 from the Japanese Embassy. The note requests Federal income tax exemption for Messrs. Sigeyoshi Sakabe and Isao Ashida, technical experts of the Japanese Foreign Office on duty with The Japan Institute at 630 Fifth Avenue, New York City. Hull provides formal certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that reciprocal tax exemption is granted by Japan to U.S. government personnel.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Sigeyoshi Sakabe and Isao Ashida
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 180 and confirms referral of tax exemption requests for Sigeyoshi Sakabe and Isao Ashida to U.S. authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note no. 180 of August 6, 1940 concerning Federal income tax exemption for Messrs. Sigeyoshi Sakabe and Isao Ashida. The two officials served as technical experts of the Japanese Foreign Office assigned to The Japan Institute in New York City. Hull informs the Ambassador that a copy of the request has been transmitted to competent U.S. authorities to effectuate the tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Ambassador Concerning Tax Exemption for Sigeyoshi Sakabe and Isao Ashida

subfiles.about: Transmits the biographical record of newly arrived Assistant Engineer Kunizi Ozawa and notifies the departures of Moritosi Maeda and Tosiyuki Mory.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador transmits to the Secretary of State the biographical record of Mr. Kunizi Ozawa, newly arrived Naval Assistant Engineer at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. The Ambassador also officially informs the Department that Naval Civil Engineer Moritosi Maeda and Naval Assistant Engineer Tosiyuki Mory were recalled to Japan and departed the United States on May 25, 1940 and July 23, 1940, respectively.
subfiles.title: Note No. 184 from the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Kunizi Ozawa, Moritosi Maeda, and Tosiyuki Mory

subfiles.about: Acknowledges certification under Section 116(h) and confirms tax exemption instructions for four naval language officers.
subfiles.from: John L. Sullivan, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of August 10, 1940 regarding Japanese Embassy Note No. 171. The letter notes the State Department's certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code regarding four language officers attached to the Japanese Naval Attaché's Office in Washington. Sullivan confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials to grant the tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Four Naval Language Officers

subfiles.about: Transmits the biographical records of Isao Ashida and Shigeyoshi Sakabe, technical experts assigned to The Japan Institute in New York City.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents his compliments to the Secretary of State and encloses biographical records for Mr. Isao Ashida and Mr. Shigeyoshi Sakabe. Both men are technical experts of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Tokyo assigned to duty at The Japan Institute in New York City. Notations indicate that the enclosures were detached for departmental records.
subfiles.title: Note No. 188 from the Japanese Ambassador Transmitting Biographical Records of Isao Ashida and Shigeyoshi Sakabe

subfiles.about: Details inquiries made to Mrs. Wenz of the Japanese Embassy to obtain biographical sketches of Ashida and Sakabe for Miss Jones.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State internal memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs records that Miss Jones had no background records for Japanese nationals Isao Ashida and Shigeyoshi Sakabe. In response, FA contacted Mrs. Wenz at the Japanese Embassy regarding the matter. The memorandum notes that biographical sketches were subsequently furnished by the Embassy and placed on file with Miss Jones.
subfiles.title: Department of State Memorandum Regarding Biographical Records of Ashida and Sakabe

subfiles.about: Requests Federal income tax exemption for Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito of the Japanese Government Railways office in New York City.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Mr. Kozo Miyabe and Mr. Ichiro Ito, secretary and clerk respectively of the Japanese Government Railways, be granted Federal income tax exemption while residing in the United States. Miyabe and Ito are assigned to the railway office at 630 Fifth Avenue, New York City, having arrived in San Francisco on May 18, 1940 aboard the steamship Tatuta Maru. The Ambassador requests that their names be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. government authorities. (Includes duplicate copy on page 115).
subfiles.title: Note No. 206 from the Japanese Ambassador Requesting Tax Exemption for Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito

subfiles.about: Encloses Japanese Embassy Note No. 206 and certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Note No. 206 from the Japanese Embassy regarding Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito. The two men serve as secretary and clerk of the Japanese Government Railways office at 630 Fifth Avenue, New York City. Hull certifies pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan extends reciprocal tax exemptions to U.S. officials performing similar duties in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 206 and confirms transmission of the tax exemption request for Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito to U.S. authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 206 of September 7, 1940 regarding Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito of the Japanese Government Railways. Hull informs the Japanese Ambassador that a copy of the note has been transmitted to competent U.S. authorities to secure their exemption from Federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Ambassador Concerning Tax Exemption for Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure of Tsutoo Takase, Secretary of the Japanese Government Railways.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State that Mr. Tsutoo Takase, Secretary of the Japanese Government Railways at 630 Fifth Avenue, New York City, will depart the United States. Takase was scheduled to leave New York on September 10 for Canada to board a steamer for Japan at Vancouver. An internal departmental notation dated September 11 indicates that the Division of Far Eastern Affairs informed Mrs. Wenz of the Japanese Embassy that the note arrived too late to process advance tax clearances.
subfiles.title: Note No. 207 from the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Departure of Tsutoo Takase

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure of Hiroshi Hara, an Education Department language officer stationed at Harvard University's Gray Herbarium.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador informs the Secretary of State of the upcoming departure of Mr. Hiroshi Hara, a language officer of the Department of Education stationed at the Gray Herbarium of Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Hara, whose income is paid entirely by the Japanese Government, is scheduled to depart from Los Angeles on October 22, 1940 aboard the Asama Maru. The Ambassador requests that his tax-exempt status be communicated to relevant U.S. government authorities.
subfiles.title: Note No. 208 from the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Departure of Hiroshi Hara

subfiles.about: Encloses Japanese Embassy Note No. 208 and certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Hiroshi Hara.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Note No. 208 from the Japanese Embassy concerning Hiroshi Hara. Hara was assigned to the Gray Herbarium of Harvard University and planned to sail from Los Angeles on October 22 aboard the Asama Maru. Hull certifies pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that reciprocal exemption privileges exist for U.S. personnel in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Hiroshi Hara
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Departmental charge slip recording the checkout of file 894.01B11 items 247 through 266 to Van Dusen.
subfiles.summary: A standard Department of State charge slip records that file 894.01B11 enclosures 247 through 266 were charged out to ES - Van Dusen on October 22, 1945. The slip contains the initials CFH.
subfiles.title: Charge Slip for File 894.01B11/247-266

subfiles.about: Acknowledges certification under Section 116(h) and confirms tax exemption instructions for Sigeyoshi Sakabe and Isao Ashida.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury replies to the Secretary of State's letter of August 27, 1940 regarding Sigeyoshi Sakabe and Isao Ashida of The Japan Institute. Acknowledging State's certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials regarding their tax-exempt status.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Sigeyoshi Sakabe and Isao Ashida

subfiles.about: Transmits the biographical record of Captain Takeo Omori, newly appointed language officer of the Imperial Japanese Army.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador presents his compliments to the Secretary of State and transmits the biographical record of Captain Takeo Omori. Omori was newly appointed as a language officer of the Imperial Japanese Army in the United States. A handwritten note indicates that the enclosure was detached for filing.
subfiles.title: Note No. 217 from the Japanese Ambassador Transmitting Biographical Record of Captain Takeo Omori

subfiles.about: Acknowledges certification under Section 116(h) and confirms tax exemption instructions for Hiroshi Hara.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of September 21, 1940 regarding Mr. Hiroshi Hara of Harvard University's Gray Herbarium. With reciprocity certified under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials regarding Hara's income tax exemption prior to his sailing from Los Angeles on October 22.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Hiroshi Hara

subfiles.about: Acknowledges certification under Section 116(h) and confirms tax exemption instructions for Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury replies to the Secretary of State's letter of October 2, 1940 regarding Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito of the Japanese Government Railways in New York City. Acknowledging certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, the Treasury states that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials to grant their Federal income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Kozo Miyabe and Ichiro Ito

subfiles.about: Requests Federal income tax exemption for Kuniji Ozawa and Yuzo Isikawa of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador requests that Mr. Kuniji Ozawa, Assistant Engineer and Assistant Inspector of Ordnance, and Mr. Yuzo Isikawa, Engineer Captain and Chief Inspector of Construction and Ordnance, be granted Federal income tax exemption. Both officers were sent by the Japanese Government for duty at the Naval Inspector's Office at 1 Madison Avenue, New York City. Ozawa arrived at Seattle on June 22, 1940 aboard the Hie Maru, and Isikawa arrived at Seattle on September 23, 1940 aboard the Hikawa Maru.
subfiles.title: Note No. 245 from the Japanese Ambassador Requesting Tax Exemption for Kuniji Ozawa and Yuzo Isikawa

subfiles.about: Encloses Japanese Embassy Note No. 245 and certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Kuniji Ozawa and Yuzo Isikawa.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Note No. 245 from the Japanese Embassy regarding Kuniji Ozawa and Yuzo Isikawa. The officers serve at the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. Hull certifies pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that the Japanese Government provides equivalent tax exemptions to American personnel in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Kuniji Ozawa and Yuzo Isikawa
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 245 and confirms transmission of the tax exemption request for Ozawa and Isikawa to U.S. authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of the Japanese Ambassador's note of October 9, 1940 regarding Kuniji Ozawa and Yuzo Isikawa of the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. Hull informs the Ambassador that a copy of the note has been forwarded to competent U.S. authorities to effectuate their exemption from Federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Ambassador Concerning Tax Exemption for Kuniji Ozawa and Yuzo Isikawa

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure from the United States of Engineer Captain Todomu Nakamura.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador notifies the Secretary of State that Mr. Todomu Nakamura, Engineer Captain and Chief Inspector of Construction and Ordnance of the Naval Technical Department, is departing the United States. Nakamura had been stationed at the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City and is scheduled to sail from San Francisco on October 21, 1940 aboard the Asama Maru. The Ambassador requests that his departure and tax-exempt status be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Note No. 246 from the Japanese Ambassador Regarding Departure of Todomu Nakamura

subfiles.about: Confirms telephone message of October 15 and certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Todomu Nakamura.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull writes to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., confirming an urgent telephone notification to the Bureau of Internal Revenue on October 15, 1940 regarding Engineer Captain Todomu Nakamura. Nakamura served at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York and scheduled his departure from San Francisco on October 21 aboard the Asama Maru. Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code to support Nakamura's tax clearance.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Todomu Nakamura
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 246 and informs the Japanese Ambassador that telephone clearance was arranged for Todomu Nakamura.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Japanese Embassy note no. 246 of October 9, 1940 regarding Engineer Captain Todomu Nakamura. Hull confirms that the information was immediately communicated by telephone to competent U.S. authorities to ensure Nakamura's exemption from Federal income tax prior to his departure from San Francisco on October 21 aboard the Asama Maru.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Ambassador Concerning Tax Exemption for Todomu Nakamura

subfiles.about: Acknowledges certification under Section 116(h) and confirms tax exemption instructions for Kuniji Ozawa and Yuzo Isikawa.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of October 24, 1940 concerning Kuniji Ozawa and Yuzo Isikawa of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. Acknowledging reciprocity certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, the Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials to grant the exemptions.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Kuniji Ozawa and Yuzo Isikawa

subfiles.about: Acknowledges certification under Section 116(h) and confirms tax exemption instructions for Todomu Nakamura.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of October 24, 1940 confirming the telephone notification of October 15 regarding Engineer Captain Todomu Nakamura. In light of the Section 116(h) reciprocity certification, Treasury confirms that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials regarding Nakamura's tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Todomu Nakamura

subfiles.about: Acknowledges certification under Section 116(h) and confirms tax exemption instructions for Judge Yorihiro Naito.
subfiles.from: John L. Sullivan, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of November 12, 1940 confirming an urgent telephone message to the Bureau of Internal Revenue on November 7 regarding Judge Yorihiro Naito. Judge Naito, who had been studying court procedure in the United States, was scheduled to sail from Los Angeles on November 16. Sullivan confirms that reciprocity under Section 116(h) was accepted and appropriate instructions issued to Internal Revenue officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Judge Yorihiro Naito

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure from the United States of Assistant Engineer Sueo Mimura.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim notifies the Secretary of State of the departure of Mr. Sueo Mimura, Assistant Engineer and Assistant Inspector of Ordnance of the Navy Technical Department at the Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. Mimura was scheduled to leave New York on November 28, 1940 and sail from San Francisco on December 11 aboard the Kamakura Maru. The Chargé requests that Mimura's name and tax-exempt status be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Note No. 292 from the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Regarding Departure of Sueo Mimura

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 5 of January 11, 1941 and confirms referral of tax exemption request for Yonosuke Tanaka to U.S. authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 5 of January 11, 1941 from the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim regarding Mr. Yonosuke Tanaka. Tanaka served as Assistant Local Secretary for Commerce and Industry of the Tokyo Commercial and Industrial Museum at 200 Madison Avenue, New York City, and planned to sail from New York on February 1 aboard the Kongo Maru. Hull confirms that a copy of the note was transmitted to competent U.S. authorities to secure Tanaka's tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Concerning Tax Exemption for Yonosuke Tanaka

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 1 and telephone notice regarding departure of Commander Tokiji Taira and instructions for obtaining his sailing permit.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 1 of January 6, 1941 and a subsequent telephone update from the Japanese Embassy on January 8 regarding Commander Tokiji Taira of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office. The note acknowledges that Taira will sail from Los Angeles on February 9 aboard the Kamakura Maru rather than January 15. Hull informs the Chargé that Taira's tax exemption request has been forwarded to U.S. authorities and that Taira may obtain his sailing permit at Room 131, Custom House, New York City.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Concerning Sailing Permit and Tax Exemption for Commander Tokiji Taira

subfiles.about: Certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Commander Tokiji Taira, Inspector of Naval Fuel Depot.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull writes to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. regarding Commander Tokiji Taira, Paymaster Commander and Inspector of Naval Fuel Depot at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. Taira planned to leave New York and sail from Los Angeles on February 9 aboard the Kamakura Maru, seeking his sailing permit before departure. Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code to grant Taira exemption from Federal income tax.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Commander Tokiji Taira
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Incomplete/damaged copy of Treasury letter acknowledging certification under Section 116(h) for Japanese Government Railways personnel.
subfiles.summary: A damaged copy of a letter from the Treasury Department to the Secretary of State acknowledging State Department certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. The letter concerns officials of the Japanese Government Railways and Board of Tourist Industry, confirming that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials regarding their tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Japanese Government Railways Personnel (Damaged Copy)

subfiles.about: Requests Federal income tax exemption for Japanese officials attached to the New York office of the Japanese Government Railways.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires presents his compliments to the Secretary of State and requests that Japanese nationals listed in an attachment be granted income tax exemption while residing in the United States. The personnel are attached to the New York office of the Department of the Imperial Japanese Government Railways at 630 Fifth Avenue. The note affirms that their compensation is derived entirely from the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Note No. 308 from the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires Requesting Tax Exemption for Japanese Government Railways Officials

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Note No. 287 and confirms referral of tax exemption request for Dr. Tokio Sasaki to U.S. authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State acknowledges receipt of Note No. 287 of November 18, 1940 from the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim concerning Dr. Tokio Sasaki. Dr. Sasaki, a professor of Kyoto Imperial University studying in the United States, sought exemption from Federal income tax on his official compensation. Hull confirms that a copy of the Embassy's note has been forwarded to competent U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Concerning Tax Exemption for Dr. Tokio Sasaki

subfiles.about: Encloses Japanese Embassy Note No. 287 and certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Dr. Tokio Sasaki.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull transmits to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr. a copy of Note No. 287 from the Japanese Embassy concerning Dr. Tokio Sasaki, a professor of Kyoto Imperial University sent to the United States for study. Hull certifies pursuant to Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code that Japan grants equivalent exemptions to U.S. personnel performing similar functions in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Dr. Tokio Sasaki
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Second page fragment of a State Department certification letter under Section 116(h) enclosing a Japanese Embassy note of January 18, 1941.
subfiles.summary: This document page is the concluding portion (page 2) of a Department of State certification letter to the Secretary of the Treasury under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code. It certifies reciprocal tax exemption for Japanese nationals named in an enclosed note from the Japanese Embassy dated January 18, 1941. Department drafting initials indicate it was prepared by FA:FM:JBJ:SS on February 5, 1941.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Reciprocal Tax Exemption (Page 2 Fragment)
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure from the United States of Commander Tokiji Taira of the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim notifies the Secretary of State of the upcoming departure of Commander Tokiji Taira, Paymaster Commander and Inspector of Naval Fuel Depot at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City. Having arrived on August 30, 1940 on the Taiyo Maru, Taira was originally scheduled to leave Los Angeles on January 15 aboard the Kamakura Maru. A departmental notation records an Embassy telephone call on January 8 changing the departure date to February 9 and requesting a sailing permit at New York City.
subfiles.title: Note No. 1 from the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Regarding Departure of Commander Tokiji Taira

subfiles.about: Encloses Japanese Embassy note and certifies tax exemption under Section 116(h) for Yonosuke Tanaka.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of State Cordell Hull writes to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., enclosing a copy of a note from the Japanese Embassy concerning Mr. Yonosuke Tanaka. Tanaka served as Assistant Local Secretary for Commerce and Industry of the Tokyo Commercial and Industrial Museum in New York City and planned to depart on February 1 on the Kongo Maru. Hull certifies reciprocal tax exemption under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Yonosuke Tanaka
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Duplicate file copy of State Department note acknowledging Note No. 5 regarding Yonosuke Tanaka.
subfiles.summary: A file carbon copy of the Secretary of State's note to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim acknowledging Note No. 5 of January 11, 1941 regarding Yonosuke Tanaka. It confirms that the request for tax exemption on Tanaka's official compensation has been referred to competent U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Concerning Tax Exemption for Yonosuke Tanaka (Duplicate)

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of State Department note acknowledging Note No. 1 and telephone notice regarding Commander Tokiji Taira.
subfiles.summary: A file copy of the Department of State's note acknowledging Note No. 1 of January 6, 1941 and subsequent telephone update concerning Commander Tokiji Taira. The note confirms that information regarding Taira's deferred departure on February 9 aboard the Kamakura Maru was forwarded to competent authorities, and indicates that Taira may obtain his sailing permit at Room 131, Custom House, New York City.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Concerning Commander Tokiji Taira (Duplicate)

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of State Department certification letter under Section 116(h) for Commander Tokiji Taira.
subfiles.summary: A duplicate copy of Secretary of State Cordell Hull's letter to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr., providing formal certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code for Commander Tokiji Taira. Taira served as Paymaster Commander and Inspector of Naval Fuel Depot at the Japanese Naval Inspector's Office in New York City and sought a sailing permit before departing Los Angeles on February 9.
subfiles.title: Letter to the Secretary of the Treasury Certifying Tax Exemption for Commander Tokiji Taira (Duplicate)
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: Acknowledges certification under Section 116(h) and confirms tax exemption instructions for four Japanese Government Railways officials.
subfiles.from: John L. Sullivan, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan acknowledges the Secretary of State's letter of January 3, 1941 transmitting Japanese Embassy Note No. 308. Sullivan confirms receipt of certification under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code regarding Seishi Ohtsuka, Jiro Tachibana, Hideo Imaizumi, and Katzuyuki Murase of the Japanese Government Railways and Board of Tourist Industry. The letter states that appropriate instructions will be issued to Internal Revenue officials to grant their Federal income tax exemptions. (Includes duplicate copy on page 158).
subfiles.title: Letter from the Treasury Department Concerning Tax Exemption for Japanese Government Railways Personnel

subfiles.about: Informs the Department of State of the scheduled departure from the United States of Dr. Tokio Sasaki of Kyoto Imperial University.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Chargé d'Affaires notifies the Secretary of State that Dr. Tokio Sasaki, a professor of Kyoto Imperial University sent by the Japanese Government for study and residing at 532 West 111th Street in New York City, will depart the United States. Sasaki, who arrived in San Francisco on June 16, 1940 on the Asama Maru, is scheduled to sail from San Francisco on December 11, 1940 aboard the Kamakura Maru. The Chargé requests that his departure and tax-exempt status be brought to the attention of appropriate U.S. authorities.
subfiles.title: Note No. 287 from the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires Regarding Departure of Dr. Tokio Sasaki

subfiles.about: Duplicate file copy of State Department note acknowledging Note No. 287 regarding Dr. Tokio Sasaki.
subfiles.summary: A file carbon copy of the Secretary of State's note acknowledging Note No. 287 of November 18, 1940 from the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim regarding Dr. Tokio Sasaki of Kyoto Imperial University. The note confirms that a copy of the Embassy's request was forwarded to competent U.S. authorities with a view to exempting Sasaki from Federal income tax on his official compensation.
subfiles.title: Note to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires ad interim Concerning Tax Exemption for Dr. Tokio Sasaki (Duplicate)
